# 金剛經注解

**ID:** X0503
**Volume:** X25
**Category:** 般若部類
**Original Category:** 大小乘釋經部／般若部疏
**Byline:** 清 孚佑帝君註解
**Dynasty:** 清
**Date:** 1644–1911
**Juans:** 1
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/X0503

## Contributors
- 孚佑帝君 (A000482)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A unique one-juan early-Qiánlóng (1736) Buddhist-Daoist syncretic *Vajracchedikā* commentary attributed to the deified [呂洞賓](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%91%82%E6%B4%9E%E8%B3%93) Lǚ Dòngbīn under his Yuán-Míng-Qīng official deification-title Fúyòu dìjūn 孚佑帝君 ("Imperial Lord of Faith-Protection"). DILA explicitly notes that this is a translator-compiler's pen-name, not literally Lǚ Dòngbīn: the work is a product of the early-Qiánlóng *fújī* 扶乩 (planchette) milieu, in which Buddhist sūtra commentaries could be produced under deity-attribution and circulated as *immortal-revealed* rather than human-authored. Prefaced 大清乾隆元年律次夾鐘之月 = Qiánlóng 1, 2nd-month = 1736-03 / 04 under the alternate name Chúnyángzǐ 純陽子 (another standard Lǚ Dòngbīn appellation). Preserved as X25 no. 503. *notBefore* / *notAfter* = 1736. Catalog dynasty 清.

**Abstract**

The preface (No. 503-A) frames the *Vajracchedikā* as the universal scripture *yǐ wúniàn wéi zōng, yǐ líxiàng wéi zhǐ, yǐ duànchú tānwàng wéi gōngfū, yǐ qīngjìng nièpán wéi jiūjìng* 以無念為宗，以離相為旨，以斷除貪妄為功夫，以清淨涅槃為究竟 ("with no-thought as its basis, with leaving-marks as its tendency, with severing greed-and-falsity as its practice, with pure nirvāṇa as its ultimate"); circulated from India to China and *jiā zhì yī biān, dǐnglǐ ér gòngfèng zhī* ("kept one volume per household, with veneration and offering"); the prefacer's disciple [黃正元](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%BB%83%E6%AD%A3%E5%85%83) Huáng Zhèngyuán (a *Mǐn-zǒngróng* 閩總戎, "Fújiàn military command," styled Tàiyī 泰一), feeling that ritual recitation without comprehension *fēi xīn zhī suǒ zhī, mù zhī suǒ àn, fēi yì zhī suǒ huì* ("not what the mind knows, the eye merely peering at the unintelligible"), invited the *Lord*'s annotation. The body of the commentary presents the sūtra in a Daoist-Buddhist syncretic register characteristic of the *fújī* tradition: terms like *xìngmìng* 性命 (nature-and-life), *qīngjìng* 清淨 (purity), and *wúwéi* 無為 (non-action) are deployed as bridge-categories.
